evidence.note: Initial plan was to inspect then 'write evaluate.py implementing all six task types' in one pass, then validate structure — no per-type implementation milestones or numeric done-checks.

Inspection was organized by task type (classification, clustering, pair, retrieval, STS, summarization), showing awareness of the 6-protocol/37-dataset hierarchy, but this was scoping not milestone planning.
Entire evaluator for all six task types written in a single monolithic pass rather than layered/ordered milestones.
Ran one representative task per type through run_eval.py — a per-type validation gesture, but the done-check was structural only, not tied to leaderboard/spec numeric agreement.
Full run + polling then submit; completion criterion throughout was '37/37 structurally valid', never a numeric per-type milestone.

reasoning: The agent grouped its inspection by task type and performed a per-type representative structural validation (step 12), lifting it above the 'vague ordering' anchor (3). But the implementation was written as one undifferentiated pass (step 7), and no milestone had a completion criterion beyond structural validity — there were no ordered, leaderboard-gated done-checks as anchor 8 requires. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, closest to 4: type-aware validation exists, but true per-type milestones with numeric done-conditions do not.
